issues.legal_issue: A transfer of land with fruit-bearing trees for their enjoyment and for planting further trees was a tenancy rather than a usufructuary mortgage where its terms and surrounding documents showed that the transfer enabled enjoyment of the land and did not secure repayment of a debt.
material_facts: The appeal arose from a suit seeking redemption of land on the claim that the transfer documents created usufructuary mortgages.
The documents transferred land with standing fruit-bearing trees for a fixed term, for enjoyment of the land and trees and for planting additional fruit-bearing trees.
The transferees paid specified consideration, could set off the land’s income against interest, and could retain possession until the consideration and the value of trees they planted were paid.
The documents were styled as kanam deeds, described the consideration as kanartham, and one expressly described the transfers as kanam-kuzhikanam.
Later documents also described the transactions as kanam-kuzhikanam.
The documents contained no recital that the transfers secured repayment of a debt and did not describe the transactions as mortgages.
issues.conclusion: The transactions were kanam-kuzhikanam leases, not usufructuary mortgages, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(23) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963, kanam-kuzhikanam includes a transfer of land, with fruit-bearing trees if any, for enjoyment of those trees and planting such trees, with the specified rights and liabilities concerning the kanartham and interest; a usufructuary mortgage as defined by section 58(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, is excluded. The essential distinction is that a lease transfers a right to enjoy property, whereas a mortgage transfers an interest in property to secure a debt. The transaction’s description by the parties is relevant but not decisive. Under section 12 of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, parties may prove that a document purporting to be a mortgage is in substance a lease; that provision does not apply where the document, properly construed, purports to be a lease. Section 2(57) includes a kanam-kuzhikanamdar within the meaning of tenant, and section 13 gives tenants fixity of tenure. No earlier cases are cited.

rule.if: redemption_suit_appeal and land_transferred_for_enjoyment and fruit_tree_planting_purpose and consideration_paid_for_transfer and income_set_off_against_interest and possession_retained_until_payment and documents_describe_tenancy and later_documents_confirm_tenancy and not documents_state_debt_security

predicates.redemption_suit_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal in a suit seeking redemption on the basis that a property transfer was a mortgage.
predicates.land_transferred_for_enjoyment: The transferor transferred land with standing fruit-bearing trees so the transferee could enjoy the land and trees.
predicates.fruit_tree_planting_purpose: The transfer allowed the transferee to plant additional fruit-bearing trees on the land.
predicates.consideration_paid_for_transfer: The transferee paid a specified amount as consideration for the transfer.
predicates.income_set_off_against_interest: The transferee could apply income from the land in lieu of interest on the consideration.
predicates.possession_retained_until_payment: The transferee could retain possession until the consideration and the value of trees planted were paid.
predicates.documents_describe_tenancy: The transfer documents described the transaction as a tenancy rather than a mortgage.
predicates.later_documents_confirm_tenancy: Later documents also described the transaction as a tenancy.
predicates.documents_state_debt_security: The transfer documents stated that the transaction secured repayment of a debt.

issues.definition: When an appeal in a redemption suit concerns a transfer made for enjoyment and tree planting, and the consideration, possession, and documents indicate a tenancy without stating that the transfer secures a debt, the transaction is a lease rather than a usufructuary mortgage.
